trust_decision.summary: Whether a patch path segment or dotted value-key segment names an existing own property of the resource (descend into it) or not (create a fresh own container); at the pinned commit both walkers follow inherited members (e.g. toString), so writes land on shared built-in function objects.

landing_point.why: The existing prototype-pollution guard (DANGEROUS_KEYS deny-list in resolvePaths, from GHSA-9m6g-wc8r-q59c) is where a reader of 'mutation of inherited built-in method objects' looks first; the tempting move is to extend that deny-list.

fix_sites.entry_point: scimPatch() add/replace/remove op with a dotted 'path' (via applyAddOrReplaceOperation src/scimPatch.ts:243 and applyRemoveOperation src/scimPatch.ts:188)

scimPatch() add/replace with no path or with an object value whose keys are dotted (src/scimPatch.ts:236 and src/scimPatch.ts:280 -> addOrReplaceAttribute -> addOrReplaceObjectAttribute src/scimPatch.ts:434-436 -> assign)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/scimPatch.ts:447-455 (assign, reached only through addOrReplaceObjectAttribute src/scimPatch.ts:425-438 when the patch value is an object with dotted keys)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report's example is a dotted 'path'; the value-object keys route looks like plain data assignment, and assign already uses a different idiom ('key in obj') that reads like a correct existence check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: (1) A falsy own intermediate (e.g. name: null) must still be replaced by a fresh container (issue #186); (2) a path like 'toString.x' must still succeed and write an own property on the resource rather than being rejected or dropped (fix.diff:116-129). Adding toString/valueOf to the DANGEROUS_KEYS deny-list or throwing on inherited names breaks (2); switching navigate to a pure hasOwnProperty-return breaks (1).

O6_input_shapes: dotted path through an inherited member (add)
path-less add with dotted value key
inherited member after an array-filter segment (emails[primary eq true].toString.x)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extractArray reads schema[attrName] without an own check; a planted variant that creates/descends a container for a non-array inherited attrName would reach the same sink via the filter-segment route
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'treat missing as add' idiom already exists for array filters at src/scimPatch.ts:254-257, so a maintainer extending it to mono-valued fallbacks is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: filter-miss add builds result[parsedPath.attrPath] from the filter's attrPath; a dotted attrPath expanded via assign-like nesting would be a parser-differential route the deny-list never sees
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Supporting sub-attribute filters (emails[type.value eq ...]) is a natural feature request for SCIM.

O9_family: prototype pollution / mutation of shared inherited objects (CWE-1321, CWE-915)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm, tsc 6.0.3, mocha 11 + chai 6, nyc
O10_build.project_tests: test/prototypePollution.test.ts (prior GHSA-9m6g tests), test/scimPatch.test.ts, test/patchValidation.test.ts; run via 'npm run mocha' (package.json:17)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add toString/valueOf/hasOwnProperty (or all Object.prototype names) to DANGEROUS_KEYS in resolvePaths and throw, which breaks the required own-property write and misses other inherited names.

out_of_scope_notes: resolvePaths deny-list compares whole segments, so '__proto__[filter]' segments bypass it at src/scimPatch.ts:171-174; it hits extractArray and appears to throw (non-iterable spread at src/scimPatch.ts:257), belongs to prior advisory GHSA-9m6g, not pursued.
